question: Can a small tensor computed only from baryonic map geometry predict normalized cluster convergence morphology, and which tiny operator changes have the largest transferable effect?

relationship_to_prior_work.p0567: P0567 proved only pointwise inverse feasibility using the target lens field. P0568 never uses a target map to construct its tensor or prediction.
relationship_to_prior_work.member_tidal_metric: Earlier member-only tidal tests scored raw multiple-image positions and selected zero coupling. P0568 is a distinct convergence-morphology compression audit; it cannot overturn that stronger raw-lensing failure.
relationship_to_prior_work.tidal_spherical_proxy: The spherical amplitude proxy already failed joint SPARC and CLASH tests. P0568 tests directional map information and retains that failure as a cross-domain comparator.
relationship_to_prior_work.novelty: No originality claim. This is a phenomenological weak-field constitutive screen.

weak_field_screen.positive_domain: Every Q_b is rescaled to spectral radius at most one and abs(t)<=0.9, so I+t*Q_b remains positive definite.
weak_field_screen.prediction: clip the first-order apparent convergence at zero and normalize it inside 250 kpc
weak_field_screen.parameters: one universal signed coupling t plus one universal source-smoothing width; no cluster-specific gravity parameters

tensor_families.field_aligned: unit traceless spin-2 tensor aligned with the Newtonian baryonic acceleration
tensor_families.gradient_aligned: unit traceless spin-2 tensor aligned with the baryonic surface-density gradient
tensor_families.tidal_full: normalized traceless Hessian of the Newtonian baryonic potential
tensor_families.tidal_low_density: tidal_full multiplied by B50/(B+B50), where B50 is the within-map positive median fixed by the baryon map
tensor_families.tidal_gradient_blend: equal pre-normalization blend of tidal_full and gradient_aligned
tensor_families.noncircular_tidal: tidal_full after subtracting its circular spin-2 mean at each radius
tensor_families.noncircular_gradient: gradient_aligned after subtracting its circular spin-2 mean at each radius
tensor_families.noncircular_blend: equal blend of noncircular_tidal and noncircular_gradient

validation.holdout_caveat: The split is prospective only to P0568; all systems are globally spent by earlier project analyses.
validation.selection: Choose one family, t, and width by minimum equal-system mean Jensen-Shannon divergence on the seven development systems only.
validation.primary_target: mean of 100 Lenstool convergence realizations after the frozen P0567 background subtraction, positive clipping, and normalization
validation.method_control: score the locked prediction against GLAFIC best maps with no reselection
validation.uncertainty: score the locked prediction against all 100 Lenstool realizations in every system

cross_domain.galaxy_data: 968 outer-holdout points in 131 SPARC galaxies with frozen inner-radius nuisance values
cross_domain.galaxy_proxy: For full tensors use spherical radial eigenvalue q=1 and K_r=1+t*S_a*q; for explicitly noncircular tensors q=0 in the axisymmetric limit. This is a conservative structural proxy, not a disk PDE solution.
cross_domain.solar_tests: maximum fractional force from 1.6 Solar radii to Saturn, Earth fraction, and first-order Mercury precession
cross_domain.comparators: fixed RAR outer RMSE 10.348 km/s; Newtonian baryon-only score is recomputed on the same frozen SPARC rows
cross_domain.noncircular_truth: The noncircular tensors are numerically checked on centered circular source maps rather than merely declared zero.

claim_limits: The baryon maps contain member-galaxy F160W light but omit hot gas and diffuse intracluster light.
Normalized convergence morphology does not test absolute lensing strength.
The target maps are standard-GR parametric lens reconstructions, not raw shear or image positions.
The field solve is first order in t and clips negative apparent-convergence pixels for comparison to the frozen positive target.
The galaxy transfer is a spherical radial proxy; only explicitly noncircular families have an exact axisymmetric null.
Earlier exact raw-lensing failure remains authoritative even if a family improves this weaker map-shape target.
